module_title: Secondary Storage - Optical Media, Magnetic Tapes, and Access Methods
introduction: This intermediate tier transitions to storage mediums that utilize lasers (Optical) and magnetic ribbons (Tapes). We also break down the two fundamental 'Data Access Methods' (Sequential vs. Direct), which frequently appear in statement-based questions.

core_concepts.title: Optical Disks
core_concepts.description: Storage devices that use a low-power 'Laser Beam' (light) to read and write data. Data is recorded on the disk's reflective surface in the form of microscopic indentations called 'Pits' (representing 0s) and flat areas called 'Lands' (representing 1s).

core_concepts.title: Standard Optical Capacities
core_concepts.description:
Examiners frequently test the maximum storage capacity of standard optical disks:
- CD (Compact Disk): Standard capacity is 700 MB.
- DVD (Digital Versatile Disk): Standard capacity is 4.7 GB (Single-layer).
- Blu-ray Disk (BD): Designed for HD video; standard capacity is 25 GB (Single-layer) to 50 GB (Dual-layer).

core_concepts.title: Magnetic Tape
core_concepts.description: A legacy storage medium consisting of a long, thin plastic ribbon coated with a magnetic material (like old audio cassettes). Today, it is exclusively used by large corporations and data centers for massive, long-term 'Data Backup' and 'Archiving'.

core_concepts.title: Data Access Methods (Sequential vs. Direct)
core_concepts.description:
- Sequential Access: Data must be read in a strict, linear physical order (e.g., Magnetic Tape). To reach the 10th file, the reader must physically pass through the first 9 files. Extremely slow.
- Direct/Random Access: The computer can jump directly to any piece of data instantly, regardless of where it is physically stored (e.g., HDD, SSD, RAM). Extremely fast.

important_entities.name: WORM
important_entities.significance: A highly tested acronym representing CD-R (Recordable) and DVD-R technology. You can permanently burn data onto the disk only once, but you can read/play it an infinite number of times. It cannot be erased.

important_entities.name: CD-RW (ReWritable)
important_entities.significance: Unlike WORM disks, a ReWritable (RW) disk allows the user to burn data, erase it, and write new data onto the same disk multiple times.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants frequently mistake CDs and DVDs for magnetic storage devices. This is a fatal error. CDs, DVDs, and Blu-rays are strictly 'Optical' (light/laser-based) devices. They contain absolutely no magnetic materials.
Magnetic Tape is the ONLY prominent storage medium that relies strictly on 'Sequential Access'. All modern storage devices (HDD, SSD, Flash) utilize Direct/Random Access.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the ascending order of optical disk capacity, use CDB: CD (700 MB) -> DVD (4.7 GB) -> Blu-ray (25+ GB).

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the full form of DVD. Examiners will offer 'Digital Video Disk' as an option to trick you. The correct and official full form is strictly 'Digital VERSATILE Disk'.
